plan: In a second‑price sealed‑bid auction, truthful bidding (bidding your private value) is a weakly dominant strategy: you win when the second‑highest bid is below your value and pay that price, maximizing expected surplus. With independent uniform values and rational opponents, bid my true value to maximize long‑run profit: 36.

[This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values. Truthful bidding is a dominant strategy: bid your value to maximize expected payoff regardless of others' strategies. No prior history to learn from, values redraw each round, and ties are random. I'll bid my true private value of 33 (allowed to one decimal place) to maximize long-run profit.]

[I will bid my true value, $31. In a sealed‑bid second‑price auction, bidding your valuation is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected payoff regardless of opponents’ actions. With independent uniform draws and 0.1 increments, shading cannot improve expected profit and may lose positive surplus. Therefore bid 31 to capture any profitable win.]
